verses.sanskrit: किं ब्रह्म किं परं धाम किं ज्ञानं किं च मोक्षणम् | किं विद्या किमविद्या च किं बन्धो मुक्तिरेव च ||
verses.transliteration: kiṃ brahma kiṃ paraṃ dhāma kiṃ jñānaṃ kiṃ ca mokṣaṇam | kiṃ vidyā kimāvidyā ca kiṃ bandho muktireva ca ||
verses.translation: What is Brahman? What is the supreme abode? What is knowledge? What is liberation? What is vidya (true knowledge)? What is avidya (ignorance)? What is bondage and what is freedom?
verses.hindi: ब्रह्म क्या है? परम धाम क्या है? ज्ञान क्या है? मोक्ष क्या है? विद्या क्या है? अविद्या क्या है? बन्धन क्या है और मुक्ति क्या है?
verses.commentary: The Niralamba opens with a barrage of the most fundamental questions — each one an entire philosophical tradition in a single word. Rather than beginning with answers, it begins with questions. This is pedagogically significant: the direct encounter with not-knowing — the willingness to stand without any support (niralamba) — is the first step of the inquiry. Spiritual development does not begin with doctrines but with the honest recognition of what one does not know.
verses.wordMeaning: The Niralamba opens with a barrage of the most fundamental questions — each one an entire philosophical tradition in a single word. This is pedagogically significant: the direct encounter with not-knowing — the willingness to stand without any support (niralamba) — is the first step of the inquiry. Spiritual development does not begin with doctrines but with the honest recognition of what one does not know.

verses.sanskrit: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते | तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ||
verses.transliteration: ananyāścintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate | teṣāṃ nityābhiyuktānāṃ yogakṣemaṃ vahāmyaham ||
verses.translation: Those who worship me with undivided mind, meditating on me without any other support — for those who are constantly united with me, I carry their welfare and security.
verses.hindi: जो लोग अनन्य भाव से मेरा चिन्तन करते हुए मेरी उपासना करते हैं — उन नित्य मुझमें संयुक्त लोगों का योगक्षेम मैं स्वयं वहन करता हूँ।
verses.commentary: Quoted within the Niralamba from the Bhagavad Gita (9.22), this verse acquires its fullest meaning in the context of "supportlessness." The one who takes no external prop — who rests solely in the Self/divine — is told: I will carry your yoga (what you need to attain) and your kshema (what you need to protect what you have). The supreme paradox: the one who releases all supports is the one most completely supported.
verses.wordMeaning: Quoted within the Niralamba from the Bhagavad Gita (9.22), this verse acquires its fullest meaning in the context of "supportlessness." The one who takes no external prop — who rests solely in the Self/divine — is told: I will carry your yoga (what you need to attain) and your kshema (what you need to protect what you have). The supreme paradox: the one who releases all supports is the one most completely supported.

verses.sanskrit: निरालम्बोऽहं निरालम्बोऽहं निरालम्बोऽहम् निरालम्बः | निरालम्बं जगत् सर्वं निरालम्बं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ||
verses.transliteration: nirālambo'haṃ nirālambho'haṃ nirālambo'ham nirālambaḥ | nirālambaṃ jagat sarvaṃ nirālambaṃ brahma śāśvatam ||
verses.translation: I am supportless, I am supportless, I am supportless, I am supportless. The world is supportless, Brahman is eternal supportless.
verses.hindi: मैं निरालम्ब हूँ, मैं निरालम्ब हूँ, मैं निरालम्ब हूँ, मैं निरालम्ब हूँ। जगत निरालम्ब है, ब्रह्म शाश्वत निरालम्ब है।
verses.commentary: The repetition of "niralamba" (supportless) is a meditative affirmation. The Self needs no support from anything outside itself. The world appears dependent, but Brahman is the supportless reality that underlies all.
verses.wordMeaning: The repetition of "niralamba" (supportless) is a meditative affirmation. The Self needs no support from anything outside itself. The world appears dependent, but Brahman is the supportless reality that underlies all.

verses.sanskrit: यो ब्रह्म वेद निरालम्बं स एव निरालम्भवान् | यो ब्रह्म न वेद निरालम्बं स दुःखार्तिर्निरालम्भः ||
verses.transliteration: yo brahma veda nirālambaṃ sa eva nirālambhavān | yo brahma na veda nirālambaṃ sa duḥkhārtirnirālambhaḥ ||
verses.translation: He who knows Brahman as supportless, he becomes supportless. He who does not know Brahman as supportless, he is the cause of suffering, supportless.
verses.hindi: जो ब्रह्म को निरालम्ब जानता है, वह निरालम्ब हो जाता है। जो ब्रह्म को निरालम्ब नहीं जानता, वह दुःख का कारण है, निरालम्ब।
verses.commentary: Knowledge of the supportless nature of Brahman liberates. Ignorance of this truth leads to suffering. The paradox: the one who does not know is also "supportless" — but in the sense of having no true foundation.
verses.wordMeaning: Knowledge of the supportless nature of Brahman liberates. Ignorance of this truth leads to suffering. The paradox: the one who does not know is also "supportless" — but in the sense of having no true foundation.

verses.sanskrit: शरीरं निरालम्बं चित्तं निरालम्बं तथा | इन्द्रियाणि निरालम्बानि ब्रह्मैव परमं निरालम्बम् ||
verses.transliteration: śarīraṃ nirālambaṃ cittaṃ nirālambaṃ tathā | indriyāṇi nirālambāni brahmaiva paraṃ nirālambam ||
verses.translation: Body is supportless, mind is supportless, senses are supportless — Brahman alone is the supreme supportless.
verses.hindi: शरीर निरालम्ब है, मन निरालम्ब है, इंद्रियाँ निरालम्ब हैं — ब्रह्म ही परम निरालम्ब है।
verses.commentary: All appearances — body, mind, senses — are ultimately without independent support. Only Brahman is truly supportless, depending on nothing.
verses.wordMeaning: All appearances — body, mind, senses — are ultimately without independent support. Only Brahman is truly supportless, depending on nothing.

verses.sanskrit: यथा स्वप्ने पश्यन्ति जाग्रति तथा पश्यति | यथा जाग्रति पश्यन्ति स्वप्ने तथा न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā svapne paśyanti jāgrati tathā paśyati | yathā jāgrati paśyanti svapne tathā na paśyati ||
verses.translation: As in dream one sees what is seen in waking, so in waking one sees what is seen in dream. But as in waking one sees what is seen in dream, so in dream one does not see.
verses.hindi: जैसे स्वप्न में वह देखता है जो जाग्रत में देखा जाता है, वैसे ही जाग्रत में वह देखता है जो स्वप्न में देखा जाता है। किंतु जैसे जाग्रत में वह देखता है जो स्वप्न में देखा जाता है, वैसे स्वप्न में वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The relationship between waking and dream states. The Upanishad points to the witness that is present in both states — the supportless awareness.
verses.wordMeaning: The relationship between waking and dream states. The Upanishad points to the witness that is present in both states — the supportless awareness.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सर्पो दृश्यते रज्जुं तथा रज्जुं दृश्यते सर्पः | यथा रज्जुं दृश्यते सर्पो न तथा सर्पो दृश्यते रज्जुम् ||
verses.transliteration: yathā sarpo dṛśyate rajjuṃ tathā rajjuṃ dṛśyate sarpaḥ | yathā rajjuṃ dṛśyate sarpo na tathā sarpo dṛśyate rajjum ||
verses.translation: As a rope is seen as a snake, so a rope is seen as a snake. But as a rope is seen as a snake, so a snake is not seen as a rope.
verses.hindi: जैसे रज्जू को साँप देखा जाता है, वैसे ही रज्जू को साँप देखा जाता है। किंतु जैसे रज्जू को साँप देखा जाता है, वैसे साँप को रज्जू नहीं देखा जाता।
verses.commentary: The classic rope-snake illusion. The error is one-sided: the rope is mistaken for snake, but the snake is never mistaken for rope. This illustrates how ignorance works — the Self is mistaken for the not-Self, but not vice versa.
verses.wordMeaning: The classic rope-snake illusion. The error is one-sided: the rope is mistaken for snake, but the snake is never mistaken for rope. This illustrates how ignorance works — the Self is mistaken for the not-Self, but not vice versa.

verses.sanskrit: यथा चाँद्रिकां दृश्यते अम्बु तथा अम्बुं दृश्यते चाँद्रिका | यथा अम्बुं दृश्यते चाँद्रिका न तथा चाँद्रिकां दृश्यते अम्बुम् ||
verses.transliteration: yathā cāṃdrikāṃ dṛśyate ambu tathā ambuṃ dṛśyate cāṃdrikā | yathā ambuṃ dṛśyate cāṃdrikā na tathā cāṃdrikāṃ dṛśyate ambum ||
verses.translation: As water is seen in a mirage, so a mirage is seen as water. But as water is seen in a mirage, so a mirage is not seen as water.
verses.hindi: जैसे मरीचिका में जल दिखाई देता है, वैसे ही मरीचिका जल के रूप में दिखाई देती है। किंतु जैसे मरीचिका में जल दिखाई देता है, वैसे मरीचिका जल के रूप में नहीं दिखाई देती।
verses.commentary: The mirage illusion. Water appears where there is none. This illustrates how the mind projects desires onto reality, creating false supports.
verses.wordMeaning: The mirage illusion. Water appears where there is none. This illustrates how the mind projects desires onto reality, creating false supports.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मृगतृष्णिका दृश्यते यथा दृश्यते तथा न तथा | यथा दृश्यते न तथा यथा न दृश्यते तथा तथा ||
verses.transliteration: yathā mṛgatṛṣṇikā dṛśyate yathā dṛśyate tathā na tathā | yathā dṛśyate na tathā yathā na dṛśyate tathā tathā ||
verses.translation: As the deer sees what is seen, so it is seen, but not so. As it is seen, not so — as it is not seen, so so.
verses.hindi: जैसे हिरण देखता है जो दिखता है, वैसा वैसा है, पर ऐसा नहीं। जैसा दिखता है, वैसा नहीं — जैसा नहीं दिखता है, वैसा वैसा।
verses.commentary: The deer chasing a mirage. The verse plays with perception and reality, pointing to the self-deception of seeking satisfaction in false supports.
verses.wordMeaning: The deer chasing a mirage. The verse plays with perception and reality, pointing to the self-deception of seeking satisfaction in false supports.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मैव तत्त्वमस्ति ब्रह्मैव परमं सुखम् | ब्रह्मैव निरालम्बं ब्रह्मैव मोक्षदायकम् ||
verses.transliteration: brahmaiva tattvamasti brahmaiva paramaṃ sukham | brahmaiva nirālambaṃ brahmaiva mokṣadāyakam ||
verses.translation: Brahman alone is the reality, Brahman alone is the supreme happiness, Brahman alone is supportless, Brahman alone is the giver of liberation.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्म ही तत्व है, ब्रह्म ही परम सुख है, ब्रह्म ही निरालम्ब है, ब्रह्म ही मोक्ष दायक है।
verses.commentary: The culmination of the Niralamba Upanishad. All attributes point to Brahman — reality, happiness, supportlessness, liberation. This is the final recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The culmination of the Niralamba Upanishad. All attributes point to Brahman — reality, happiness, supportlessness, liberation. This is the final recognition.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तिं गच्छतु शान्तिं गच्छतु शान्तिं गच्छतु शान्तिम् | शान्त्येव परमं ब्रह्म शान्त्येव परमं निरालम्बम् ||
verses.transliteration: śāntiṃ gacchatu śāntiṃ gacchatu śāntiṃ gacchatu śāntim | śāntyeva paraṃ brahma śāntyeva paraṃ nirālambam ||
verses.translation: Go to peace, go to peace, go to peace, go to peace. Peace alone is supreme Brahman, peace alone is supreme supportless.
verses.hindi: शांति में जाओ, शांति में जाओ, शांति में जाओ, शांति में जाओ। शांति ही परम ब्रह्म है, शांति ही परम निरालम्ब है।
verses.commentary: The closing peace chant. Peace is identified with Brahman and the supportless reality. The repetition is an invitation to rest in that peace.
verses.wordMeaning: The closing peace chant. Peace is identified with Brahman and the supportless reality. The repetition is an invitation to rest in that peace.
